problem_statement: The ttntm/11ty-landing-page project is an Eleventy and Tailwind marketing landing page. Its Features section presents six AWE.SOME product features as shadowed cards (local SVG icon, uppercase heading, and paragraph). The section carries a native 'Feature focus' filter: a row of All / Launch / Automate / Measure tabs above the six feature cards, plus a live '#featfilter-readout' count that reports how many of the six features are showing ('Showing N of 6 · <Focus>'). The same 'Feature focus' filter bar is promoted on the home page Features section AND on a shared /highlights/ page that reuses the section, so a visitor can narrow the feature set by the outcome they care about on either surface. The filter feature has regressed on four orthogonal axes and must be repaired together. (1) The filter tab row is laid out as a fixed-width, non-wrapping flex track, so on a 390px mobile viewport it is wider than the phone screen and the whole page overflows horizontally. (2) The filter bar's 'Feature focus' title is no longer promoted across both surfaces (it is missing from the /highlights/ page). (3) The filtered card grid has broken layout: instead of a tidy multi-column grid the cards are pulled together with negative margins so they shingle and overlap into an illegible pile, and the filter tabs and readout are styled as near-white text on near-white pills and near-black text on the dark section so the controls and card copy are unreadable. (4) Clicking a focus tab marks the tab active and hides the non-matching cards but leaves the '#featfilter-readout' count stale ('Showing 6 of 6 · All focuses'), so the post-click state is wrong. Repair the filter tab row so it wraps with no mobile overflow, restore the 'Feature focus' title on both the home and /highlights/ surfaces, restore the tidy multi-column grid with legible on-brand tabs and card copy, and wire the tab clicks so the readout re-syncs to 'Showing N of 6 · <Focus>' — all without altering the feature card copy, the local icons, the navigation, the hero/about/register sections, the privacy/imprint routes, or the Eleventy/Tailwind build pipeline.
required_content: The 'Feature focus' filter tab row must fit within a 390px mobile viewport so the page no longer overflows horizontally on the home and /highlights/ routes (no_horizontal_overflow within 24px tolerance).
The 'Feature focus' title bar must be promoted on the Features section of BOTH surfaces: the home page and the shared /highlights/ page. It must not be shown on only one of them.

The filtered feature grid must render as a tidy multi-column card grid (no overlapping/shingled cards), and the filter tabs, active tab, and readout must be legible on-brand controls (readable text on the blue section) matching the captured reference states — not a collapsed overlapping grid with illegible near-white-on-near-white tabs.

Clicking a focus tab (for example Automate) must re-filter the grid to show only the matching cards AND re-sync the #featfilter-readout count to 'Showing N of 6 · <Focus>' (for example 'Showing 2 of 6 · Automate'); marking the tab active and hiding cards is not sufficient.

The six feature cards (Instant Onboarding, Live Automations, Insight Dashboards, Guarded Access, Signal Routing, Cohort Reports) with their local feature icons, uppercase headings, focus labels, and copy must remain exactly as authored; only responsive layout, cross-page presence, grid/tab layout, and filter wiring change.

Desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) keep the multi-column feature grid and the 'Feature focus' filter bar with no horizontal overflow, and the six feature cards continue to render on the home and /highlights/ routes.
The fix must not regress the hero, About, Registration form, footer, privacy/imprint routes, local logo, GitHub icon, feature icons, or the shared navbar and mobile menu.
design_constraints: Treat this as a design-continuity extension/repair of the Features section's own 'Feature focus' filter (mobile overflow + cross-page presence + grid/tab layout + filter wiring), not a visual redesign of the landing page.

Use the existing shadowed-card Tailwind style, blue/purple/gray palette, tracking-wide uppercase headings, and rounded purple controls; keep the feature cards, their icons, focus labels, and copy unchanged.

The filter tab-row overflow repair and the tidy-grid / legible-tab repair live in src/_includes/css/featfilter.css. The cross-page presence repair lives in src/_data/focusnav.js (which surfaces render the 'Feature focus' title). The tab-click filter + readout wiring repair lives in src/_includes/js.njk. Do not alter the feature card data/markup, the local assets, or the page structure.

The feature-card content and surrounding landing-page DOM must remain identical to the reference; only the responsive overflow behavior, the surfaces the filter title renders on, the grid/tab layout, and the filter wiring change.

Ground the repair in the captured visual states: the reference desktop/mobile Features screenshots show the 'Feature focus' filter bar with legible on-brand tabs over a tidy multi-column grid, and after clicking Automate the grid shows the two Automate cards with the readout 'Showing 2 of 6 · Automate'.
state_constraints: desktop_home, mobile_home, and tablet_home verify the home Features section, the 'Feature focus' filter bar, its legible on-brand tabs, and the tidy multi-column grid of six feature cards across viewports.
desktop_highlights, mobile_highlights, and tablet_highlights verify the same feature grid and the shared 'Feature focus' title bar are promoted on the /highlights/ page (cross-page presence).

features_filter scrolls to the home Features section, clicks the Automate focus tab, and verifies the grid re-filters to the two Automate cards and the #featfilter-readout re-syncs to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Automate' (the interaction terminal state).
mobile_nav_open clicks the mobile menu button and verifies the shared navbar stays available.
The mobile states (mobile_home, mobile_highlights, mobile_nav_open) are the horizontal-overflow discriminator: the reference reports 0 overflow while the fixed-width tab row overflows.

change_completion: The 'Feature focus' filter tab row wraps responsively so the home and /highlights/ routes have no horizontal overflow at 390px (within 24px tolerance).

The filter title is promoted on both the home and /highlights/ surfaces, the grid renders tidily with legible on-brand tabs, and clicking a focus tab re-filters the grid and re-syncs the #featfilter-readout count.
design_consistency: The repaired filter bar and card grid keep the existing shadowed-card, blue/purple/gray, uppercase-heading, and rounded-control style; the grid is not a collapsed overlapping pile and the tabs/readout are legible.
The change extends the AWE.SOME landing-page visual system rather than introducing a foreign or standalone UI surface.
responsive: On a 390px mobile viewport the filter tab row fits inside the Features section so the document has no horizontal overflow (within 24px tolerance).
Desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) keep their multi-column feature grid and 'Feature focus' filter bar with 0 overflow.
regression: Hero, About, Registration form, footer, privacy/imprint routes, local logo, GitHub icon, feature icons, and the shared navbar remain intact.
The Eleventy build/serve continues to work without new dependencies.
state_coverage: Captured states cover the home Features section across desktop, tablet, and mobile, the shared /highlights/ page across desktop, tablet, and mobile, the mobile navbar, and the Automate-tab filter interaction.

metadata.design_goal: extend the local visual system and shared navigation through a consistent feature-focus filter built from the existing card, heading, and control components
metadata.source_repo_kind: Eleventy/Tailwind marketing landing page with a shared base layout, data-driven navbar, structured section data, a native feature grid, and local SVG assets.
metadata.selected_repo_reason: ttntm/11ty-landing-page is a runnable Eleventy/Tailwind marketing landing page that builds to static output offline and hosts a natural design-continuity feature filter on the Features section's own grid, spanning a mobile-overflow defect, cross-page presence, filtered-grid layout, and tab-click wiring.

author_notes: L4 design-continuity task on the ttntm 11ty-landing-page marketing site, built so the lever is the landing page's OWN Features section and its native 'Feature focus' category filter (All / Launch / Automate / Measure over six real feature cards with local SVG icons and a live count), hardened to fail four orthogonal acceptance gates in the bad solution. Lever 1 (D6 no_horizontal_overflow): the filter tab row uses a fixed-width non-wrapping track that overflows a 390px viewport; the reference wraps it. Lever 2 (D2 dom_assertions, cross-page): the 'Feature focus' title bar must be promoted on the home Features section AND the shared /highlights/ page; the reference promotes it on both, the baseline and bad only on the home surface (missing on /highlights/). Lever 3 (D3 visual_regression): the bad filtered grid collapses — the cards are pulled together with negative margins so they shingle and overlap into an illegible pile, the active tab is near-white on near-white, and the card copy is near-black on the dark blue section — failing pixelmatch/ssim/block fidelity against the tidy reference grid. Lever 4 (D4 interaction_assertions): the bad tab click marks .is-active and hides cards but never re-syncs #featfilter-readout, so the post-click count stays 'Showing 6 of 6 · All focuses'. Three leg-varying files (src/_includes/css/featfilter.css, src/_data/focusnav.js, src/_includes/js.njk) live in suggested_files; the feature-card data/markup and local image assets are byte-identical across legs. Built offline as static Eleventy output with that infrastructure identical across legs.
